slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Try to define "point" and you need other words, like "location". Define those and you are soon back where you started. Every definition uses earlier words, so some words must stay undefined: point, line and plane.

In the same way, every proof uses earlier facts, so some statements must be accepted without proof. These are postulates (also called axioms). For example: through any two points there is exactly one line. Everything else is built from undefined terms, definitions, and postulates.
